speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you've been experiencing a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me understand your condition better, have you noticed if the rash appears in streaks or clusters on your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola)

The progression of symptoms—starting with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache followed by a rash that spares the perioral area—is classic for measles. I will request a serum test for measles IgM antibodies to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Measles_IgM
